teaser.text: Marathon Petroleum Corporation, or MPC, is a large fuel and infrastructure business. It buys crude oil, turns it into fuels and materials, and moves hydrocarbons to customers.

stock.opening: The probability-weighted price is $373.78 in October 2027 and $332.34 in October 2029; the bear case has a 25% probability, the base case 60%, and the bull case 15%. It hinges on whether exceptional refining margins persist.
stock.closing: The full MPC memo also explains MPC’s business, its rivals, its management and its risks.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for MPC, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The bear case gives $8,000 million in 2027 and $8,500 million in 2028. It reaches $9,500 million in 2029 as operations recover. This reflects rapid margin normalization, RIN expense and turnaround costs; MPC spent $1,514 million on refining turnarounds in 2025. The bull case gives $15,000 million in 2027 and $14,000 million in 2028. It falls to $12,500 million in 2029, remaining below the 2022 peak because even a favorable cycle should fade.

blocks.heading: How much cash does MPC really make?

paragraphs.text: MPC generates substantial cash, but capital spending, working capital and future obligations determine what remains. Operating cash flow was $8,253 million in 2025. After $3,486 million of capital spending, free cash flow was $4,767 million.

MPC’s calculation becomes more conservative after deducting $160 million of stock compensation. That treats employee shares as an economic cost to existing owners, although it is not another cash payment during the year.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for MPC today?

paragraphs.text: The P/E ratio compares the share price with annual earnings, but refining earnings move with crack spreads—the gap between the value of fuels and the crude used to make them. MPC’s refining margin was $36.33 per barrel in the second quarter of 2026, versus $17.58 a year earlier. That improvement helps explain why a low forward P/E may depend on unusually favorable conditions.

blocks.heading: How much does MPC pay in dividends over time?

paragraphs.text: The dividend base case holds at $4.00 per share through 2027, then rises to $4.20 and $4.41. The current quarterly rate is $1.00, and annual dividends rose in every year of the supplied 2021–2025 history. The bear case cuts the payout to $3.80 and then $3.60 as free cash flow weakens. The bull case reaches $4.20, $4.62 and $5.08, supported by the prior 10% rate increase and MPLX distribution growth.

blocks.heading: Does MPC’s cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: MPC generates substantial cash, but capital spending, working capital and future obligations determine what remains. Operating cash flow was $8,253 million in 2025. After $3,486 million of capital spending, free cash flow was $4,767 million.

The pressure became clearer in 2024. Shareholder payments reached $10,343 million against free cash flow of $6,132 million, or 168.7%. MPC also paid $1,377 million to minority owners. MPC controls MPLX, so it includes MPLX’s full business in its consolidated accounts, but outside MPLX investors own part of the profits. Consolidated cash is therefore not all available to MPC shareholders.

earnings.title: MPC earnings date and guidance
earnings.meta_description: MPC reports next on November 3, 2026; guidance covers capital, throughput and refining costs.
earnings.opening: MPC's next results are expected on November 3, 2026. Watch whether throughput, routine costs, turnaround expense and cash after working-capital changes match guidance.
earnings.closing: The full memo explains MPC's business, rivals, management and risks.

paragraphs.text: MPC’s capital outlook, excluding MPLX, is $1.5 billion. About 65.0% targets value-enhancing projects and 35.0% supports existing operations, which means management is improving the refinery network without planning a major expansion of capacity.

MPLX carries the larger growth plan. Its growth capital outlook is $2.9 billion, with at least 90.0% directed toward natural gas and natural gas liquids infrastructure. NGLs are liquids such as propane and butane recovered alongside natural gas. Management expects those investments to support 12.5% annual distribution growth in each of the next two years.

The near-term operating test is refinery execution. MPC guided throughput of 3,005 thousand barrels a day at routine refining costs of $5.60 per barrel for the third quarter. It separately allowed $290 million for turnarounds, planned shutdowns for major maintenance. A plant can meet its volume target while losing cash through repair costs and lost production.

blocks.heading: What has MPC's revenue and profit trend been over the last eight quarters?

paragraphs.text: Second-quarter 2026 was a powerful refining-margin quarter. Revenue reached $52,337 million, up 53.5% from the prior-year quarter. Diluted EPS rose from $3.96 to $17.73.

The main change was value earned per refining barrel. Refining & Marketing margin rose from $17.58 to $36.33 per barrel. Utilization was 94%, compared with 97% a year earlier, so the earnings surge did not require a matching increase in plant activity.
